## SEO Agent — Page Watch (G11, v4.16)
Runs **every day at 05:45** (n8n's clock) and on demand through *Watch Run* (`{ domain | site_id, finding_key? }`; the web app uses it for a single re-check). Free: one plain **GET** per key page plus `/robots.txt`, no JavaScript, no paid API, at most 25 pages a site.
**The key pages** come from the one site model and the page inventory `seo_pages` (home page, the menu, the pages Search Console brings impressions for, the published ladder pages, the AI pages) — never a fresh crawl.
**What is watched:** HTTP status, a redirect that appeared, `noindex` (meta or `X-Robots-Tag`), the canonical, the `<title>`, and the fingerprint of `/robots.txt` (`seo_cache` key `watch:<site_id>`, beside the sitemap fingerprints). Also stored for the re-checks: the meta description and the H1s. A change that matters raises an alert **the same day** in `seo_console_alerts` (`kind: page_watch` — the app's Alerts page and the Monday report read it); a page gone, noindexed, blocked or re-canonicalised also goes to `seo_ops_alerts` and to `SEO_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack / Teams, no SMTP), deduped as D25b dedupes. A fetch that failed is **not checked**: the stored reading stays, nothing is claimed.
**"I fixed this"** (criterion 1.10): the app sets `seo_audit_findings.recheck_state = requested`; the next run judges that finding on the pages it just read and writes back `fixed`, `still_open`, or `not_checked` with the reason it needs the full audit. Rules: `v5/code/_page_watch.js`.
**Google's view** of the same pages (`seo_page_watch.inspect_*`) is written by the weekly Site Tracker: URL Inspection rotates through every key page, oldest first, inside Google's 2,000-a-day quota (G25).
